answer_text:
We use Taylor expansions about \(z=0\).

\[
\sin z = z-\frac{z^3}{6}+O(z^5)
\]

So

\[
\sin^2 z
= \left(z-\frac{z^3}{6}+O(z^5)\right)^2
= z^2-\frac{z^4}{3}+O(z^6).
\]

Also,

\[
\cos z \sin z=\frac{1}{2}\sin(2z)
= z-\frac{2z^3}{3}+O(z^5).
\]

Thus

\[
z\cos z\sin z
= z^2-\frac{2z^4}{3}+O(z^6).
\]

Now expand the numerator:

\[
\begin{aligned}
12z^2+6\sin^2 z-18z\cos z\sin z
&=12z^2+6\left(z^2-\frac{z^4}{3}+O(z^6)\right) \\
&\quad -18\left(z^2-\frac{2z^4}{3}+O(z^6)\right) \\
&=12z^2+6z^2-2z^4-18z^2+12z^4+O(z^6) \\
&=10z^4+O(z^6).
\end{aligned}
\]

For the denominator,

\[
\sin^4 z = \left(z+O(z^3)\right)^4 = z^4+O(z^6).
\]

Therefore,

\[
\frac{12z^2+6\sin^2z-18(\cos z\sin z)z}{\sin^4 z}
=
\frac{10z^4+O(z^6)}{z^4+O(z^6)}.
\]

Dividing numerator and denominator by \(z^4\),

\[
\frac{10+O(z^2)}{1+O(z^2)} \to 10
\qquad \text{as } z\to 0.
\]

Hence,

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
